messages:
anya: quick triage — I'm bootstrapping emberlyn-6b for eval + PTQ experiments. upstream archive includes a header that calls the license 'Research-Only v0.9' and requires attribution. unsure whether quantized derivatives are allowed to be redistributed or served in Dedicated/Private.

sam: summary of perf so far — float fp16 baseline perplexity 12.4, 4-bit PTQ (int4 blockwise) ppx 14.7, and we see a small but consistent drop on our summarization eval (ROUGE-L -3.2). hallucination rate up ~5% on our factual QA.

anya: repro command for the PTQ run I used:
```bash
python quantize.py --model emberlyn-6b --method block-wise-int4 --calib-samples 1024 --out emberlyn-6b-int4.tar.gz
```
cle o: tiny nit: can you paste the exact license text? sometimes the headline and the embedded clauses differ.

anya: pasted from LICENSE.txt in the tarball: "Research-Only v0.9
You may use this model for internal research and evaluation. Redistribution of original or derivative model weights is prohibited without express permission. Attribution required for published results."

marta: thanks. +1 to legal review. initial read: explicit "redistribution of original or derivative model weights is prohibited" sounds restrictive — likely blocks embedding quantized weights in downloads or sharing with customers.

marta: clarifying q's for triage: (1) is emberlyn provided under any dual-license or FOSS exception? (2) did upstream include a CLA that permits commercial hosting? (3) are we planning to surface weights to customers (Dedicated/Private) or only serve via hosted API?

anya: answers: (1) no dual license in repo, just that single LICENSE.txt; (2) contributor list shows corporate contributors but no CLA file; (3) goal was to offer it as an experimental model in Hosted first, but some POCs wanted to deploy to Dedicated pools and private on-prem for pilot customers.

josh: operational note — from infra side, serving the quantized binary in Dedicated (we keep the artifacts on our disks) vs shipping it as a bundle to a customer's on-prem deployment are different: the latter is effectively redistribution.

deploy-bot: Automated scan complete: license flag = research-only; artifact redistribution = prohibited; recommend legal approval before any external distribution. [scan id: SB-2026-039] :warning:

marta: given the wording, we should NOT distribute quantized weights to customers or include them in any downloadable offering. Hosting in our Hosted API for internal evaluation may be acceptable under "internal research and evaluation" but that's borderline if customers can directly query it — need to confirm scope.

sam: from a product perspective, we can do limited internal eval + gated A/B tests behind feature flags. if we surface it in Hosted API, we must ensure we don't provide a direct binary or SDK that exposes raw weights. also watch attribution clause for public benchmarks.

cleo: QA request — add the emberlyn prompt-set to regressions and flag the tests where PTQ regresses more than 2%. I'll open a small PR with the eval vectors.

anya: next steps I propose: 1) legal (marta) confirm whether hosting behind our API counts as "redistribution"; 2) we freeze any plan to ship artifacts to customers; 3) run more calibration-aware PTQ (L2 calibration, per-channel) to try to close the quality gap; 4) if still regress, request permission from upstream or drop the model from public offerings.

marta: agreed. I'll ask legal to draft a short memo: determine whether "hosting as a service" violates the redistrib clause and whether attribution-only use (with no weight transfer) is allowed. Also will ask whether a written permission request to upstream maintainers is feasible and what language to seek.

sam: technical ask — can we run a quick eval comparing PTQ with quant-aware finetune (QAT) as a potential mitigation? if we can avoid redistribution by only serving via Hosted and still get acceptable quality, that's a path forward.

anya: yes, queued QAT run starting now — I'll post results to the internal eval dashboard: https://redwood.internal/evals/emberlyn-6b/ (link for team only).

josh: operationally, if legal says hosting is ok, we should still add a footprint tag to the model page: "redistribution prohibited" so Dedicated/private onboarding automatically blocks downloads and export.

marta: noted. I'll also confirm whether requiring attribution in customer-facing docs is compatible with enterprise contracts.

anya: thanks all — leaving the thread for legal to update. ping me for any missing artifacts (I'll attach the quantized tarball to the legal ticket but won't share it externally until we get sign-off). :thumbsup:

marta: received — starting review.

deploy-bot: Reminder: do not promote emberlyn-6b to public model catalog until manual legal approval noted in model metadata.

sam: ack.

cleo: will add the emberlyn vectors to the regression suite by EOD.

anya: closing the loop here, will update when QAT results land (expect ~4-6h).
